Source: https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/prepare-for-the-databricks-data-engineer-associate-certification-exam-and-pass/

Prepare for the Databricks Data Engineer Associate Certification exam and pass!

We just posted a new course from Andrew Brown on the freeCodeCamp.org YouTube channel that will help you earn the Databricks Data Engineer Associate Certification. This course is designed to take you from a foundational understanding of data to building and managing production-grade data pipelines.

The Databricks Certified Data Engineer Associate certification exam assesses an individual’s ability to use the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform to complete introductory data engineering tasks. This includes an understanding of the Data Intelligence Platform and its workspace, its architecture, and its capabilities. It also assesses the ability to perform ETL tasks using Apache Spark SQL or PySpark, covering extraction, complex data handling and User defined functions. Finally, the exam assesses the tester’s ability to deploy and orchestrate workloads with Databricks workflows configuring and scheduling jobs effectively.

This free course is an all-in-one resource for preparing for the Databricks Data Engineer Associate Certification. It combines theoretical knowledge with practical, hands-on skills, ensuring you’re ready to pass the exam and tackle real-world data engineering challenges.

Course topics include:

- Introduction
- Data Basics
- Data Models Processing
- Data Integrity
- Data Sources
- Introduction to Databricks
- Cluster Types
- Databricks Web Application
- Version Control
- Delta Lake
- Spark DataFrame API
- Table and Views
- SQL Commands and Logic
- File Handling and Formats
- Structured Streaming
- Auto Loader
- Delta Live Table
- Jobs Monitoring and Visualization
- Unity Catalog
- Access Control

Watch the full course on the freeCodeCamp.org YouTube channel (7.5-hour watch).

reference_note.title: Databricks Data Engineer Associate Certification - Course Overview
reference_note.summary: This course prepares learners for the Databricks Data Engineer Associate Certification by covering foundational data engineering concepts and practical skills needed to build production-grade data pipelines on Databricks. The exam assesses ability to use the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform, perform ETL tasks with Apache Spark SQL or PySpark, and deploy and orchestrate workloads with Databricks workflows. The course combines theoretical knowledge with hands-on practice across data modeling, Delta Lake, Spark APIs, streaming, and access control.

key_concepts.simple_explanation: A unified platform that combines data warehousing, data lakes, and machine learning capabilities. It includes a workspace where you can write code, manage data, and build pipelines.
key_concepts.why_it_matters: Understanding the platform's architecture and capabilities is foundational to using Databricks effectively in any real project

key_concepts.simple_explanation: The process of pulling data from sources (Extract), modifying it to meet requirements (Transform), and storing it in a target location (Load). This is a core data engineering task.
key_concepts.why_it_matters: Most real-world data projects involve ETL workflows; Databricks is designed to make this easier with Spark SQL and PySpark

key_concepts.simple_explanation: Tools for processing large amounts of data in parallel. Spark SQL uses SQL syntax, while PySpark uses Python. Both run on Databricks clusters.
key_concepts.why_it_matters: These are the primary languages for writing data transformations and handling complex data operations in Databricks projects

key_concepts.simple_explanation: A way to schedule and orchestrate jobs (automated tasks) that run on a schedule or trigger. Allows you to automate data pipelines.
key_concepts.why_it_matters: In production projects, you need to automate data processing; workflows handle scheduling and job management

key_concepts.simple_explanation: A storage layer built on top of data lakes that adds reliability, performance, and ACID transactions to data stored in cloud object storage.
key_concepts.why_it_matters: Delta Lake is Databricks' recommended format for storing data; it ensures data quality and consistency in production pipelines

key_concepts.simple_explanation: Different configurations of compute resources (servers) that run your Spark jobs. Different types are optimized for different workloads.
key_concepts.why_it_matters: Choosing the right cluster type affects cost, performance, and how quickly your data processing completes

key_concepts.simple_explanation: A centralized governance system for managing access to data and metadata across Databricks workspaces.
key_concepts.why_it_matters: In enterprise projects, you need to control who can access what data; Unity Catalog provides this control

key_concepts.simple_explanation: Mechanisms to restrict who can view, modify, or execute code and data in Databricks.
key_concepts.why_it_matters: Real projects require security; you need to ensure only authorized users can access sensitive data

important_features_or_tools.name: Databricks Workspace
important_features_or_tools.what_it_does: A collaborative environment where data engineers write code, manage notebooks, organize files, and build data pipelines
important_features_or_tools.when_to_use_it: Every time you work in Databricks; it's the main interface for development and collaboration

important_features_or_tools.name: Spark DataFrame API
important_features_or_tools.what_it_does: A programmatic interface for working with distributed data using Python or Scala. Allows you to manipulate large datasets efficiently.
important_features_or_tools.when_to_use_it: When you need to perform complex transformations or when SQL is not sufficient for your data processing logic

important_features_or_tools.name: Tables and Views
important_features_or_tools.what_it_does: Tables store actual data; Views are virtual tables that query existing tables. Both can be queried with SQL.
important_features_or_tools.when_to_use_it: Tables for storing persistent data, Views for creating reusable query logic without duplicating data

important_features_or_tools.name: Structured Streaming
important_features_or_tools.what_it_does: Allows you to process continuous streams of data in real-time using the same Spark API as batch processing
important_features_or_tools.when_to_use_it: When you need to process data that arrives continuously (e.g., sensor data, logs, event streams)

important_features_or_tools.name: Auto Loader
important_features_or_tools.what_it_does: Automatically detects and ingests new files from cloud storage as they arrive, without manual intervention
important_features_or_tools.when_to_use_it: When you have data arriving continuously in cloud storage and want to automatically load it into Databricks

important_features_or_tools.name: Delta Live Table
important_features_or_tools.what_it_does: A declarative way to define data pipelines using SQL or Python. Automatically manages dependencies and data quality.
important_features_or_tools.when_to_use_it: When building production data pipelines that need automatic dependency management and quality checks

important_features_or_tools.name: Jobs
important_features_or_tools.what_it_does: Automated tasks that run code on a schedule or trigger. Used to orchestrate data pipelines in production.
important_features_or_tools.when_to_use_it: When you need to run data processing tasks automatically on a schedule (e.g., daily, hourly)

important_features_or_tools.name: Databricks Web Application
important_features_or_tools.what_it_does: The browser-based interface for accessing Databricks. Provides UI for notebooks, clusters, jobs, and data management.
important_features_or_tools.when_to_use_it: For all interactions with Databricks, including writing code, managing resources, and monitoring jobs

important_features_or_tools.name: Version Control
important_features_or_tools.what_it_does: Integration with Git systems to track changes to code and collaborate with team members
important_features_or_tools.when_to_use_it: In team projects where multiple engineers work on the same codebase and need to track changes

important_features_or_tools.name: Monitoring and Visualization
important_features_or_tools.what_it_does: Tools to track job execution, view logs, and visualize data pipeline performance and results
important_features_or_tools.when_to_use_it: When running production jobs to ensure they complete successfully and to debug failures

practical_workflow.action: Understand the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform architecture and workspace structure
practical_workflow.reason: You need to know how Databricks is organized before you can use it effectively

practical_workflow.action: Learn data basics and data models relevant to your project
practical_workflow.reason: Good data engineering starts with understanding your data structure and quality requirements

practical_workflow.action: Set up a cluster and learn cluster types available
practical_workflow.reason: You need compute resources to run any Spark jobs; choosing the right type affects cost and performance

practical_workflow.action: Learn to write SQL commands and Spark code (PySpark or Spark SQL) for data transformation
practical_workflow.reason: These are the primary tools for ETL tasks in Databricks

practical_workflow.action: Understand Delta Lake and how to store data in Delta format
practical_workflow.reason: Delta Lake is the recommended storage format for production data in Databricks

practical_workflow.action: Learn to create and manage Tables and Views for your data
practical_workflow.reason: Tables and Views organize your data and make it queryable by your team

practical_workflow.action: Build ETL pipelines using Spark DataFrame API or SQL, handling complex data and user-defined functions
practical_workflow.reason: This is the core work of data engineering; you need to extract, transform, and load data reliably

practical_workflow.action: Learn file handling and data formats (CSV, Parquet, JSON, etc.)
practical_workflow.reason: Real projects involve reading and writing data in various formats from different sources

practical_workflow.action: Explore Structured Streaming and Auto Loader for continuous data ingestion
practical_workflow.reason: Many modern projects require real-time or near-real-time data processing

practical_workflow.action: Learn Delta Live Tables for building production-grade pipelines
practical_workflow.reason: Delta Live Tables simplify pipeline management and add automatic quality checks

practical_workflow.action: Set up Jobs and Workflows to schedule and orchestrate your pipelines
practical_workflow.reason: Production pipelines must run automatically on a schedule; Jobs handle this

practical_workflow.action: Implement access control and learn Unity Catalog for data governance
practical_workflow.reason: Real projects require security and governance; you need to control who accesses what data

practical_workflow.action: Use monitoring and visualization tools to track job execution and troubleshoot issues
practical_workflow.reason: Production pipelines need monitoring to ensure they run successfully and to debug failures

common_mistakes_or_confusions.mistake: Thinking Databricks is only for big data or large-scale projects
common_mistakes_or_confusions.correction: Databricks is useful for any data engineering project, regardless of scale. Start small and scale as needed.

common_mistakes_or_confusions.mistake: Confusing Tables and Views; thinking they store data the same way
common_mistakes_or_confusions.correction: Tables store actual data; Views are virtual and query existing tables. Use Views to avoid data duplication.

common_mistakes_or_confusions.mistake: Not understanding the difference between batch processing and streaming
common_mistakes_or_confusions.correction: Batch processing handles data in chunks at scheduled times; Streaming processes continuous data in real-time. Choose based on your use case.

common_mistakes_or_confusions.mistake: Ignoring data quality and integrity from the start
common_mistakes_or_confusions.correction: Data quality is critical in production. Use Delta Lake and Delta Live Tables to enforce quality checks early.

common_mistakes_or_confusions.mistake: Manually running data pipelines instead of automating with Jobs
common_mistakes_or_confusions.correction: Always automate production pipelines with Jobs and Workflows. Manual execution is error-prone and doesn't scale.

project_usage_notes: Start by setting up a Databricks workspace and cluster. Choose a cluster type appropriate for your workload (e.g., all-purpose for development, job for production).
Store all your data in Delta Lake format. This ensures ACID transactions and data reliability in production.
Use Delta Live Tables to define your ETL pipelines declaratively. This reduces boilerplate code and adds automatic quality checks.
Implement Jobs and Workflows to schedule your pipelines. Never rely on manual execution in production.
Use Unity Catalog and access control from the start to ensure data governance and security, even in small projects.
Monitor your jobs using Databricks' monitoring and visualization tools. Set up alerts for failures.
Use version control to track changes to your code. Collaborate with team members using Git integration.
For real-time data, use Structured Streaming and Auto Loader to automatically ingest new data as it arrives.
Test your pipelines thoroughly before deploying to production. Use separate development and production clusters.
Document your data models, transformations, and pipeline logic. This helps team members understand and maintain your code.

source_content:
The Databricks Certified Data Engineer Associate certification exam assesses an individual’s ability to utilise the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform to execute foundational data engineering tasks. The exam assesses the test takers’ knowledge on the Data Intelligence Platform, its workspace, architecture, and capabilities, the tasks related to Data Ingestion, Data Loading, Data Transformation and Modelling- such as the ability to perform Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) tasks using PySpark, working with Lakeflow Jobs, and CI/CD. Finally, the exam assesses the test takers’ understanding of troubleshooting, monitoring, and optimization techniques, as well as their knowledge of achieving Governance and Security within the Databricks Platform.

The exam covers:

- Databricks Intelligence Platform - 6%
- Data Ingestion and Loading - 21%
- Data Transformation and Modeling - 22%
- Working with Lakeflow Jobs - 16%
- Implementing CI/CD - 10%
- Troubleshooting, Monitoring, and Optimization - 10%
- Governance and Security - 15%

**Type: **Proctored certification

**Total number of scored questions: **45

**Time limit: **90 minutes

**Registration fee: **$200

**Question types: **Multiple choice

**Test aides: **None allowed

**Languages: **English, 日本語, Português BR, 한국어

**Delivery method: **Online or test center

**Prerequisites: **None, but related training highly recommended

**Recommended experience: **hands-on experience performing the data engineering tasks outlined in the exam guide.

**Validity period: **2 years

**Recertification: **Recertification is required every two years to maintain your certified status. To recertify, you must take the current version of the exam. Please review the “Getting Ready for the Exam” section below to prepare for your recertification exam.

**Unscored content: **Exams may include unscored items to gather statistical information for future use. These items are not identified on the form and do not impact your score. Additional time is factored into the exams to account for this content.

- Review the Data Engineer Associate Exam Guide to understand what will be on the exam
- Take the related training outlined in the Exam Guide
- Use the AI Prep Guide to prepare
- Register for the exam
- Review the technical requirements for taking an online proctored exam and run a system check
- Review the exam guide again to identify any gaps
- Study to fill in the gaps
- Take your exam!

Data manipulation code in this exam is provided in SQL when possible. In all other cases, code will be in Python.

To register for a certification exam, please log in or create an account on our exam delivery platform.

Unity Catalog is the unified governance layer for both data and AI in Databricks. It provides a single place to control access, track lineage, discover assets, monitor quality, and govern AI across your organization, no matter where your data lives.

This chapter covers governing data and AI assets with Unity Catalog. Related security topics, such as authentication, networking, encryption, and privacy compliance, are covered in Security and compliance.

The following resources help you understand Unity Catalog, set it up, and follow recommended practices.

-
- What is Unity Catalog?
- Understand the Unity Catalog object model and how it governs data and AI assets.

-
- Get started with Unity Catalog
- Set up Unity Catalog and create your first governed assets.

-
- Unity Catalog best practices
- Follow recommended practices for setting up and managing governance with Unity Catalog.

The following capabilities cover the major areas of governing data and AI assets with Unity Catalog.

-
- Access control
- Grant and manage fine-grained access to data and AI assets with privileges, attribute-based access control, and row filters and column masks.

-
- Governed tags
- Define and control the tags used to classify and organize securable objects.

-
- Data discovery
- Help users find the data and AI assets they need with Catalog Explorer, AI-generated comments, and certified and deprecated tags.

-
- Data lineage
- Capture and visualize how data flows through your organization, down to the column level.

-
- Data classification
- Automatically scan and tag sensitive data, such as PII, across tables in Unity Catalog.

-
- Data quality monitoring
- Detect anomalies across a catalog or schema and profile the statistical properties of individual tables.

-
- Auditing
- Track who accessed your data and what actions they took using system tables and audit logs.

-
- Data sharing
- Share data and AI assets securely across organizations and platforms with OpenSharing, Clean Rooms, and Databricks Marketplace.

-
- AI governance
- Extend Unity Catalog access control, lineage, and auditing to AI assets and AI traffic.

reference_note.title: Unity Catalog: Unified Governance for Data and AI
reference_note.summary: Unity Catalog is Databricks' central governance layer that lets you control access, track data flow, discover assets, monitor quality, and govern AI in one place. It works across your entire organization regardless of where your data lives. As a new user, you need to understand that Unity Catalog is the foundation for managing who can access what data and how that data moves through your organization.

key_concepts.simple_explanation: A single governance system in Databricks that manages permissions, tracks data movement, helps people find data, monitors data quality, and controls AI usage across your entire organization.
key_concepts.why_it_matters: In a real project, you need to ensure the right people access the right data, know where data comes from, and can find what they need. Unity Catalog handles all of this centrally.

key_concepts.simple_explanation: Data and AI objects (like tables, models, dashboards) that are managed and controlled through Unity Catalog's governance rules.
key_concepts.why_it_matters: When you create tables or AI models in Databricks, you want them governed so access is controlled, changes are tracked, and quality is monitored.

key_concepts.simple_explanation: The ability to decide who can see, read, or modify specific data and AI assets using permissions called privileges.
key_concepts.why_it_matters: In any real project, sensitive data must be restricted to authorized users only. Unity Catalog lets you grant fine-grained permissions.

key_concepts.simple_explanation: A record of how data flows through your organization—showing which tables feed into which analyses, down to the individual column level.
key_concepts.why_it_matters: When something goes wrong with your data, lineage helps you trace the problem back to its source and understand the impact.

key_concepts.simple_explanation: Tools and features that help users find the data and AI assets they need by searching, browsing, and reading descriptions.
key_concepts.why_it_matters: In a large organization, people need to know what data exists and where to find it. Discovery tools save time and reduce duplicate work.

important_features_or_tools.name: Access control
important_features_or_tools.what_it_does: Lets you grant and manage fine-grained permissions to data and AI assets using privileges, attribute-based access control, row filters, and column masks.
important_features_or_tools.when_to_use_it: When you need to restrict who can access specific tables, rows, or columns—for example, hiding salary data from non-HR users or restricting regional data to regional teams.

important_parameters.meaning: Specific permissions like SELECT, MODIFY, or MANAGE that control what users can do with an asset
Access rules based on user attributes or data attributes rather than individual user names
Rules that automatically hide certain rows from users based on conditions
Rules that hide or redact sensitive column values for certain users

important_features_or_tools.name: Catalog Explorer
important_features_or_tools.what_it_does: A UI tool that helps users browse and discover data and AI assets available in Unity Catalog.
important_features_or_tools.when_to_use_it: When you or your team need to find existing tables, models, or other assets without knowing their exact names.

important_features_or_tools.name: Governed tags
important_features_or_tools.what_it_does: Lets you define and control standardized tags used to classify and organize securable objects (tables, models, etc.).
important_features_or_tools.when_to_use_it: When you want to label assets with consistent metadata—for example, tagging tables as 'PII', 'Production', or 'Deprecated' so users understand their sensitivity and status.

important_features_or_tools.name: Data lineage
important_features_or_tools.what_it_does: Captures and visualizes how data flows through your organization, showing which tables and columns feed into which analyses and models.
important_features_or_tools.when_to_use_it: When you need to understand data dependencies, troubleshoot data quality issues, or assess the impact of changing a table.

important_features_or_tools.name: Data classification
important_features_or_tools.what_it_does: Automatically scans tables in Unity Catalog to detect and tag sensitive data like personally identifiable information (PII).
important_features_or_tools.when_to_use_it: When you have large datasets and need to identify sensitive columns automatically rather than manually reviewing each table.

important_features_or_tools.name: Data quality monitoring
important_features_or_tools.what_it_does: Detects anomalies across catalogs or schemas and profiles the statistical properties of individual tables to track data health.
important_features_or_tools.when_to_use_it: When you need to monitor whether your data is staying within expected ranges and alert on unusual patterns that might indicate problems.

important_features_or_tools.name: Auditing
important_features_or_tools.what_it_does: Tracks who accessed your data and what actions they took using system tables and audit logs.
important_features_or_tools.when_to_use_it: When you need to answer questions like 'Who accessed this sensitive table?' or 'What changed in this dataset?' for compliance or troubleshooting.

important_features_or_tools.name: Data sharing
important_features_or_tools.what_it_does: Lets you securely share data and AI assets across organizations and platforms using OpenSharing, Clean Rooms, and Databricks Marketplace.
important_features_or_tools.when_to_use_it: When you need to share datasets with external partners or other organizations without copying data or losing governance.

important_parameters.meaning: A method for sharing data across Databricks workspaces and organizations
A secure environment for sharing and analyzing data with external parties
A platform for discovering and sharing datasets and AI assets

important_features_or_tools.name: AI governance
important_features_or_tools.what_it_does: Extends Unity Catalog's access control, lineage tracking, and auditing capabilities to AI assets and AI traffic.
important_features_or_tools.when_to_use_it: When you're building AI models and need to control who can access them, track which data they use, and audit how they're being used.

important_features_or_tools.name: AI-generated comments
important_features_or_tools.what_it_does: Automatically generates descriptions for data assets to help with discovery.
important_features_or_tools.when_to_use_it: When you want to improve data discovery by having automatic descriptions of tables and columns without manual documentation effort.

important_features_or_tools.name: Certified and deprecated tags
important_features_or_tools.what_it_does: Special tags that mark assets as certified (trusted, production-ready) or deprecated (no longer recommended for use).
important_features_or_tools.when_to_use_it: When you need to guide users toward reliable data sources and away from outdated or unreliable ones.

practical_workflow.action: Understand the Unity Catalog object model by reading 'What is Unity Catalog?' documentation
practical_workflow.reason: You need to know how Unity Catalog organizes and governs data before you can set it up or use it effectively.

practical_workflow.action: Set up Unity Catalog in your Databricks workspace using the 'Get started with Unity Catalog' guide

practical_workflow.action: Monitor data quality and set up auditing to track access and changes
practical_workflow.reason: Ongoing monitoring ensures data stays healthy and you can detect unauthorized access or unexpected changes.

practical_workflow.reason: Lineage helps you troubleshoot issues and understand data dependencies.

common_mistakes_or_confusions.mistake: Thinking Unity Catalog is only for security or only for data discovery
common_mistakes_or_confusions.correction: Unity Catalog is a unified governance layer that handles access control, discovery, lineage, quality, auditing, and AI governance all together. It's not just one thing—it's a complete governance platform.

common_mistakes_or_confusions.mistake: Assuming Unity Catalog only works with data stored in Databricks
common_mistakes_or_confusions.correction: Unity Catalog can govern data and AI assets 'no matter where your data lives'—it's designed to work across your entire organization, including external data sources.

common_mistakes_or_confusions.mistake: Setting up access control without thinking about data discovery
common_mistakes_or_confusions.correction: Access control and discovery work together. You need to restrict access to sensitive data AND help users find the data they're allowed to see. Both matter in a real project.

common_mistakes_or_confusions.mistake: Not using data classification and lineage until there's a problem
common_mistakes_or_confusions.correction: Set up data classification and lineage early in your project. They're much more valuable for prevention and understanding than for troubleshooting after issues occur.

project_usage_notes: In a real Databricks project, start by setting up Unity Catalog early—don't wait until you have governance problems. It's easier to govern from the beginning than to retrofit governance later.
Use access control to implement the principle of least privilege: give users only the permissions they need for their role. This reduces risk and keeps sensitive data safe.
Apply data classification automatically to identify PII and other sensitive data. This is especially important if you're working with customer or employee data.
Set up auditing from day one. It helps with compliance, troubleshooting, and understanding who's using your data.
Use data lineage to document how your project's data flows. This is invaluable when you need to explain data dependencies to stakeholders or troubleshoot unexpected results.
Tag your assets consistently (e.g., 'Production', 'Staging', 'Deprecated') so team members know which data to trust and use.

If you're sharing data with external teams or partners, use data sharing features (OpenSharing, Clean Rooms, or Marketplace) instead of copying data. This keeps governance intact and reduces duplication.
If your project includes AI models, extend governance to those models using AI governance so you can track which data they use and who accesses them.

source_content:
Unity Catalog is the unified governance layer for data and AI built into Databricks. When enabled for a workspace, Unity Catalog operates beneath every data and AI interaction in your workspaces automatically: enforcing access control when you query a table or call a model, tracking lineage as data and AI assets are used, logging activity for auditing, and more. You work with the objects Unity Catalog governs through Catalog Explorer, SQL, the Databricks CLI, and REST APIs.

Unity Catalog is automatically enabled for all Databricks workspaces created after November 8, 2023.

- To verify that Unity Catalog is enabled and set up properly for your workspace, see Unity Catalog setup guide.
- If your workspace was created before November 8, 2023, see Upgrade a Databricks workspace to Unity Catalog.

Unity Catalog is also available as an open-source implementation. See the announcement blog and the public Unity Catalog GitHub repo.

Every asset you govern in Unity Catalog is modeled as a **securable object**, an object on which you can grant permissions to users, service principals, or groups. Data and AI assets such as tables, views, volumes, functions, models, and services (model services and MCP services) follow a three-level namespace (`catalog.schema.object`). Tables and volumes can be **managed**, where Unity Catalog handles both governance and the underlying file storage lifecycle, or **external**, where Unity Catalog handles governance only. Other objects, such as storage credentials, external locations, connections, and shares, sit directly under the metastore.

The following pages explain core Unity Catalog concepts and workflows in more detail.

-
- Securable objects
- Learn about each object type in the Unity Catalog hierarchy and how permissions apply to them.

-
- Managed versus external assets
- Understand the difference between managed and external tables and volumes, and when to use each.

-
- Requirements and limitations
- Review compute requirements, supported file formats, naming constraints, and known limitations.

Unity Catalog provides built-in tools for governing every dimension of your data and AI environment. The following topics cover the major capability areas.

-
- Access control
- Manage who can access what using privileges, attribute-based policies, row and column filters, and workspace bindings.

-
- Discovery
- Interact with securable objects using Catalog Explorer, the Databricks UI for discovering and managing data and AI assets registered in Unity Catalog.

-
- Lineage
- Automatically track how data and AI assets flow and connect, from source data through to models, services, and dashboards.

-
- Auditing
- Maintain a complete record of all data access and system activity using the audit log system table.

-
- Data classification
- Automatically classify and tag sensitive data in your catalog.

-
- Data quality monitoring
- Proactively track data health with built-in profiling and alerts that catch anomalies before they reach downstream consumers.

-
- Data sharing
- Securely share live data and AI assets across organizations and clouds using the open OpenSharing protocol.

-
- AI governance
- Govern AI assets and AI traffic using Unity Catalog and AI Gateway.

The following resources help you get started with Unity Catalog. If your workspace was created after November 8, 2023, it is automatically enabled with Unity Catalog.

-
- Get started with Unity Catalog
- Check if Unity Catalog is already enabled for your workspace, and configure your first catalog, schema, and data access controls.

-
- Upgrade to Unity Catalog
- Learn how to upgrade a workspace that is not yet using Unity Catalog.

-
- AI governance guide
- Set up governance for your AI assets, AI traffic, and AI service behavior.

Attribute-based access control (ABAC) is an access control model in Unity Catalog where access is determined by evaluating **attributes** associated with securable objects. These attributes, represented through governed tags, are used in **policy** conditions to identify which data a policy should protect.

Policies are attached at a level in the Unity Catalog hierarchy, such as a catalog, schema, or table, and are evaluated dynamically. When a securable object has the attributes targeted by a policy, that policy takes effect automatically, so a single policy can enforce consistent access rules across an entire catalog or schema.

ABAC supports row and column-level security through row filter policies and column mask policies on tables, materialized views, and streaming tables. ABAC also supports dynamic privilege grants through GRANT policies (Beta), currently scoped to `EXECUTE` on models.
